sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the western part of Clementon, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north straight up the page. Blackwood Avenue crosses the sheet from west to east just below its middle, and Chews Landing Avenue runs diagonally above it, from the upper left towards the lower right, where it meets Blackwood Avenue beyond the east edge (sheet 3 continues there). North of Chews Landing Avenue the streets are Naylor Avenue (also lettered Tomblin Avenue) at the west edge, Forrest, Edison, Fulton, Monmouth and Trenton Avenues running north and south, an unnamed lane parallel to Chews Landing Avenue, a second lane at the upper right and Barber Avenue at the east edge. These blocks hold scattered frame dwellings with many coops, stables and wagon sheds, and large lots still open. South of Blackwood Avenue lies a regular grid laid out in narrow lots: Holly, Laurel, Birch and Elm Roads run north and south, crossed by Princeton Road, with Cedar Lane running diagonally to the south-east and Indian Spring Road cutting across the lower right corner. This grid is only partly built, with a few dozen frame dwellings, mostly near Blackwood Avenue and along Indian Spring Road; block 19 at the west and the strip of deep lots south of Cedar Lane are almost empty. Two concrete-block buildings stand on the lots between Chews Landing and Blackwood Avenues. A water pipe laid in 1909 is noted along Chews Landing Avenue, and the west margin is marked as vacant beyond and with no exposure. There are no industrial premises or institutions on the sheet; it is an area of small new houses on the edge of the town.
notes: Blackwood Avenue is now Blackwood-Clementon Road; Chews Landing Avenue is Chews Landing Road; Princeton Road is Princeton Avenue; Elm Road is Elm Avenue.
Naylor Avenue is lettered with Tomblin Avenue in brackets as its other name.
The Blackwood Avenue / Forrest Avenue junction was rejected by the fit (12 m): modern Forrest Avenue meets Blackwood-Clementon Road off its 1924 line.

Western Clementon: Blackwood Av, Chews Landing Av, Naylor (Tomblin) Av, Forrest, Edison, Fulton, Monmouth, Trenton Avs; Holly, Laurel, Birch, Elm Rds, Princeton Rd, Cedar Lane, Indian Spring Rd. 100 ft, north up. One part. Pilot sheet. Scanned narrower than the rest (8179 px wide), so px_per_ft is about 3.78 against 3.94 elsewhere.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of Clementon, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up the page. The Atlantic City Railroad crosses the sheet as a bundle of tracks from the upper left to the lower right, with Atlantic Avenue alongside it on the west and East Atlantic Avenue at the foot of the sheet. West of the tracks, Chews Landing Avenue and Blackwood Avenue run in from sheet 2; Trenton, Barber and Brighton Avenues bound a block of lots (block 28) north of them, and the Clementon Mill and Lumber Company, with long lumber sheds, a planing mill and lumber piles, occupies the ground above Barber Avenue. South of Blackwood Avenue are the blocks laid along Wauseon Avenue, Adams Avenue, Elm Road and Princeton Road, with a small plumbing shop on Princeton Road and Indian Spring Road at the lower left. East of the tracks, Berlin Road crosses from left to right through the commercial centre: the Clementon Inn, a post office, a row of brick stores, the Clementon National Bank, St. Mark's Church and a public school stand along or near it, and a cement bridge carries it over the creek. Gibbsboro Road leaves Berlin Road diagonally to the north-east, with Lincoln and Garfield Avenues laid out in long narrow lots above it, mostly built with frame dwellings. A Public Service Railway right of way runs beside them. At the right edge Park Boulevard, Roosevelt Avenue and White Horse Avenue (Clementon Road) lead to the Park Hotel, a feed warehouse and other buildings at the entrance to Clementon Park. Clementon Lake fills the lower right corner. The scale bar and the sheet number are at the foot.
notes: Blackwood Avenue is now Blackwood-Clementon Road; Chews Landing Avenue is Chews Landing Road; Princeton Road is Princeton Avenue; Elm Road is Elm Avenue.
Lakewood or Erial Avenue is Erial Road or Clementon-Erial Road today.
Modern Brighton Avenue south of Barber Avenue lies about 36 m west of the drawn street at Chews Landing Road, so that junction was not used.
Modern Berlin Road / Park Boulevard falls about 12 m east of where the sheet draws Park Boulevard meeting Berlin Road; a hand-picked point there was left out because it worsened the fit.

Central Clementon: Chews Landing and Blackwood Avs, Trenton, Barber, Brighton Avs, Lincoln, Garfield, Gibbsboro Rd, Berlin Rd, Park Blvd, the Atlantic City Railroad; 100 ft, north up. One part. Brighton Av south of Barber and Berlin Rd / Park Blvd left out (modern lines 36 m and 12 m off).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the north-eastern part of Clementon village and the amusement ground of Clementon Park, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned: north points to the upper right at about 35 degrees. The top left is Clementon Park on the shore of Clementon Lake, with a penny arcade, Ferris wheel, kiddies' air planes, knock out and skooter concessions, an ice cream pavilion, a carrousel, a bath house with dance hall, booths, a roller coaster loop, and an entrance drive and park entrance reaching the road at the upper right. Berlin Road enters from the top left, passes the park entrance and then descends the sheet as the main street of the village, with Lake Avenue parting from it to the west. Along Berlin Road the blocks are narrow lots with frame dwellings, a fire company house, a Red Men's Hall, a bake shop, a boarding house and the Clementon Community Church. Trout Run Road leaves it at the upper right with lots on its south side, a Private Lane, and a large bath house beside Silver Lake. Across the east side the lots of Bungalow, Erie and Higgins Avenues and Harvard Terrace are laid out in long strips, mostly unbuilt. At the lower left, Niagara, Central and Etlon Avenues and Saratoga and Switzerland Terraces serve a scatter of houses at Pilling's Park, with a dance hall and bath house on Pillings Lake. Blocks 41 to 48 and 194 to 197 are numbered. Streams and lake outlines are tinted blue; the adjoining sheets are 3, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 11.
notes: Higgins Avenue is lettered with (Forrest) in brackets as its other name.
Berlin Road, Lake Avenue, Niagara Avenue, Etlon Avenue, Wilson Avenue, Delaware Avenue and Higgins Avenue keep their names today; Trout Run Road is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Control is weak: three detected junctions and two hand-picked ones (Berlin Road / Lake Avenue and Etlon Avenue / Wilson Avenue), all on the southern two thirds of the sheet except one.
Modern Delaware Avenue lies 5 to 8 m from the drawn street (its junctions were left out of the fit).
The 1924 Clementon Park buildings and roller coaster have no modern control; the park is placed from the streets alone.

Clementon Park with Berlin Rd, Lake, Niagara, Etlon, Delaware, Higgins (Forrest) Avs; turned about +36 deg. 100 ft. One part. Weak control (3 automatic and 2 hand-picked points); Delaware Av left out as displaced.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the open country north and north-west of Clementon village, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 32 degrees, with north toward the upper left. White Horse Pike crosses the top of the sheet as a straight street lined with narrow lots (block 141) holding a row of frame dwellings. Below it the White Horse Avenue diagonal runs from the upper left to the lower right, with Oak Lane branching up to the right from it and Silver Lake Drive leaving Oak Lane to the south-east. A fan of long thin lots (block 146) is laid out between Oak Lane and White Horse Avenue, almost all empty, and a smaller group around Mt. Vernon, Harding and Glen Avenues (blocks 145 and 144) has only a few houses and a water pipe in Glen Avenue. At the right edge California Avenue and a second stretch of Silver Lake Drive, Ohio Avenue and Gibbsboro Road continue onto sheet 6, with block numbers 147 to 150. The lower third is crossed by a stream with a bridge at the right edge, with Sibylline Place on its north bank and a footbridge near the centre; Garfield Avenue runs along the south side of the stream, with lots 51 to 77 beside it, and the Atlantic City Railroad and Atlantic Avenue cut the lower left corner. Park Boulevard is marked at the right edge. Much of the sheet is blank paper, belonging to farmland or to the adjoining sheets.
notes: White Horse Pike is also called South White Horse Pike in OpenStreetMap.
The sheet is turned: the compass shows north towards the upper left, and the fit gives a rotation of about -32 degrees.
Glen Avenue / White Horse Avenue was excluded: the modern node falls about 15 m from the drawn junction.
The lower left (Garfield Avenue, Lincoln Avenue, Atlantic Avenue and the stream) has no control point and rests on extrapolation of the fit.

White Horse Pike, White Horse Av, Oak Lane, Silver Lake Drive, Mt. Vernon, Harding, Glen, California, Garfield and Atlantic Avs; turned about -32 deg. 100 ft. One part. Lower left and the Pike row have no control.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the Silver Lake and Spring Lake plots north of Clementon, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 31 degrees, north toward the upper left. The top is bounded by White Horse Pike, with Franklin, Watson, Knight, United States and Brand Avenues running off it to the north on sheet 8. The main body is a regular grid of 50 foot streets laid out for lots: Gibbsboro Road at the left edge and Pennsylvania, Washington and White Avenues run one way, crossed by Ohio Avenue, Silver Lake Drive and Spring Lake Avenue, enclosing blocks 157 to 170 divided into narrow numbered lots. The plots are nearly all empty; the buildings are a garage with a capacity of 50 cars at the upper left, a handful of frame dwellings in blocks 159, 160 and 163, and the Silver Lake Inn and other buildings at the upper right. Ohio Avenue and Silver Lake Drive continue east as dashed streets marked not opened, with White Avenue turning at the right. Trout Avenue runs down the right edge beside Trout Run and Silver Lake. In the lower left the White Horse Avenue diagonal (marked Clementon Road) passes the Clementon Spring Water Company's pumping station and a row of dwellings, with Roosevelt Avenue branching off it, around the edge of Bottom's Lake. At the bottom right Berlin Road runs along a row of buildings, among them a movie house and a factory, up to Trout Run Road and Lake Avenue. A compass rose and a scale bar appear in the lower middle.
notes: Spring Lake Avenue is Spring Lake Drive today; White Horse Avenue is the road lettered with Clementon Road in brackets.
Berlin Road / Lake Avenue and Berlin Road / Trout Avenue were not detected; the lower right rests on the fit from the grid above.

Silver Lake and Spring Lake plots: Gibbsboro Rd, Pennsylvania, Washington, White, Ohio Avs, Silver Lake Drive, Spring Lake Av; Berlin Rd and Bottom's Lake at the foot; turned about -31 deg. 100 ft. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the Watsontown district on the north-east side of Clementon, along the White Horse Pike between Brand Avenue on the west and Atlantic Avenue on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. The Pike crosses the sheet from left to right; along it stand scattered frame dwellings and stables, a service station with gasoline pumps near the east end, and a few outbuildings, with the lot lines of blocks 183, 184 and 192 reaching back from it. At the top left, Brand Avenue runs along numbered lots 15 to 40 with a few dwellings, and Hurilla Avenue, a short 50 foot street with houses on both sides, lies across the top middle. Read Avenue, 40 feet wide, runs diagonally from the top towards the Pike, and Atlantic Avenue, 50 feet wide, runs down the right side with a regular row of lots and dwellings on both sides. South of the Pike Higgins Avenue and Trout Avenue run south, and Ohio Avenue crosses them above blocks 185 and 186, with a brook crossing the strip of lots to its north. Below Ohio Avenue the sheet shows the subdivision of blocks 186 to 190 between Silver Lake and Higgins (Forest) Avenue, cut by Harding, Hoffman, Barry, Worrel and Hook Avenues, which are 35 feet wide and mostly unbuilt; a few frame dwellings stand on Barry Avenue. A creek runs down the left centre and Rowand's Lake appears at the bottom right corner beside the scale bar. A large part of the sheet to the east of Higgins Avenue and south of the Pike is blank.
notes: Read Avenue is Reed Avenue in OpenStreetMap, and Worrel Avenue is Worrell Avenue.
Modern Reed Avenue and Atlantic Avenue meet the White Horse Pike 9 and 24 m from where the sheet draws Read and Atlantic Avenues; both were left out of the control.
Higgins Avenue jogs where it crosses Ohio Avenue on the sheet, as the two OpenStreetMap nodes of the Higgins and Ohio junction do; both were used.
The stream at the left centre is lettered Run; the lake lettering south-west of block 190 reads Silver Lake. A foot bridge crosses the water at Barry Avenue.

Watsontown: White Horse Pike from Brand Av to Atlantic Av, Higgins (Forest), Ohio, Trout Avs and the Harding to Hook Av subdivision; north up-left (-27 deg). 100 ft. One part. Read Av and Atlantic Av at the Pike left out (modern nodes 9 and 24 m off).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the north-east edge of Clementon, between Gibbsboro Road on the west and Brand Avenue on the east, with the White Horse Pike along its foot. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Most of the sheet is open ground divided into numbered blocks 151 to 156. West of Gibbsboro Road a few frame dwellings and stables stand beside the road in blocks 251 and 252. Cooper Avenue crosses the left side, with a row of small lots and dwellings along its north side and a large undivided block, 152, to the south. Franklin Avenue, Watson Boulevard and Knight Avenue run up the page from the Pike as narrow strips of long, deep lots, mostly empty on the Franklin side and built up with frame dwellings along Watson Boulevard and Knight Avenue. A diagonal line cuts across the page above them and bounds the built part. East of Knight Avenue the blocks are empty until United States Avenue, a 50 foot street lettered not open, and then Brand Avenue, 35 feet wide, with a regular row of narrow lots on its west side. A 6 inch water pipe from the Springs Water Company runs along Gibbsboro Road and Cooper Avenue. Along the Pike are lots 401 to 423, a few dwellings, and, south of it, the ends of Pennsylvania, Washington, White and Trout Avenues, which belong to sheets 5 and 6. The compass and the scale bar fill the empty upper and lower parts of the sheet.
notes: Gibbsboro Road is East Gibbsboro Road in OpenStreetMap north of the Pike.
United States Avenue is drawn here as a paper street (lettered not open) and is not the modern United States Avenue, which lies about a kilometre to the east; it was not used.
Knight Avenue and the Pike were not detected as a junction; the other eight control points lie along the Pike, Gibbsboro Road, Cooper Avenue and Franklin Avenue.

Gibbsboro Rd to Brand Av along the White Horse Pike: Cooper, Franklin, Watson, Knight Avs; United States Av drawn as not open (a paper street, not today's United States Av); north up-left (-32 deg). 100 ft. One part; northern 60 percent mostly blank and without control.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the area west and north-west of Clementon Lake, where Erial Avenue (lettered Lakewood or Erial Avenue) runs diagonally across the page between the Atlantic City Railroad on the east and the edge of Clementon Heights on the south-west. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. The upper left holds blocks 60 to 68, long narrow lots between Davis, Woodland, Scott and Audubon Avenues; those on Scott and Audubon Avenues are largely empty, and Audubon Avenue is lettered not open. Along Erial Avenue stand scattered frame dwellings with names written beside them, among them Fairview, Pine Lodge, Oak Villa, The Laurel and Coseynook, and a tile works near the top right. Highland Avenue runs parallel to Erial Avenue below it through blocks 65 and 66, with a few dwellings and outbuildings. Atlantic Avenue runs beside the railroad, which carries several tracks across the right centre, and East Atlantic Avenue, also lettered Lake Drive, follows the lake side of the tracks past lots of small cottages and clubhouses on the lake shore. Clementon Lake and its creek arms fill the right and bottom right. At the lower left, Stanert, Sitley, Grove, Spring, Ivy and Forrest Avenues lie in blocks 69 to 74 and the subdivision called Lake View Park, mostly vacant, with a few frame dwellings. A stand pipe of the Clementon Spring Water Company, 55 feet high with a capacity of 19,000 gallons, stands at the left edge with its water mains, and the sheet joins sheets 3, 4, 10 and 12.
notes: Erial Avenue is Erial Road in OpenStreetMap (Clementon-Erial Road further south); East Atlantic Avenue keeps its name.
Stanert, Grove, Spring, Ivy and Forrest Avenues are not in OpenStreetMap on these lines; Sitley Avenue and Terrace Avenue survive near the lower left corner.

Placed by a four-point similarity along Erial Road only (Davis, Woodland, Scott and Audubon Avenues); an overlay of the modern streets shows Highland, Sitley and East Atlantic Avenues falling on their drawn lines, but no control point lies off Erial Road.
Audubon Avenue is lettered not open on the sheet; Grove Avenue appears again, lettered vertically, at the bottom left edge.

Lakewood or Erial Av with Scott, Audubon, Woodland, Davis, Highland, Sitley Avs, the Atlantic City Railroad, East Atlantic Av and Clementon Lake; north points right (+73 deg). 100 ft. One part, helmert from four junctions on Erial Rd only.

sheet-10-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 10, the larger part, covers Pine Grove on the south-east side of Clementon, between the Atlantic City Railroad and Pilling's Lake, together with a corner of the town north of it next to sheets 9 and 12. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right of the page; a heavy line along the railroad separates it from the Watsontown part on the left. At the top, Spring Avenue, Grove Avenue, Ivy Avenue, Forrest Avenue, Lakeview and Atlantic Avenue bound blocks 75, 76 and 77, which hold a few frame dwellings; below them lie the golf grounds of the Pine Valley Country Club. The Atlantic City Railroad runs diagonally down the middle of the part with several tracks. East of it, East Atlantic Avenue runs along the railroad, and from it Point Breeze Avenue, Albertson Avenue, Palethorp Avenue, Overington Avenue, Palmetto Avenue and Sepviva Avenue run east towards the lake through blocks 1 to 8 of narrow, deep lots. Building is sparse: rows of small one-storey frame dwellings along the lake shore and on Point Breeze and Albertson Avenues, a dance pavilion near Point Breeze Avenue and scattered dwellings further south; block 7 is empty. Clementon Lake, a picnic ground, a wooden bridge and the long arms of Pilling's Lake fill the right half of the part, with a public road along its far shore.
notes: Palethorp Avenue is now Palethorpe Avenue and Palmetto Avenue is Palmetta Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The streets of the top corner (Spring, Grove, Ivy, Forrest Avenues and Lakeview) do not survive on their old lines and gave no control.
The word Park is lettered across block 77 between Spring and Atlantic Avenues.

Three control points are modern parcel block corners at the east ends of Palethorp and Overington Avenues; East Atlantic Avenue is measured with a 50 ft width because the detector paired its east edge with the railroad tracks.

Two parts separated by a heavy line along the railroad, both turned with north to the right (about +72 to +77 deg). Part 1 (right, larger): Pine Grove, East Atlantic Av with Point Breeze, Albertson, Palethorp, Overington, Palmetto, Sepviva Avs, Clementon and Pilling's Lakes, Pine Valley Country Club golf grounds; top corner (Spring, Grove, Ivy, Forrest Avs, Lakeview) has no surviving junctions. Part 2 (left strip): Watsontown on the White Horse Pike, Atlantic Av, New Freedom Rd, Rd to Lucastion (United States Av). 100 ft.
placenames: Pine Valley Country Club Golf Grounds

sheet-10-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 10 is a narrow strip on the left of the sheet showing Watsontown, the settlement along the White Horse Pike north-east of Clementon. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right of the page; a heavy line separates it from the Pine Grove part on the right. The White Horse Pike runs down the strip with a 6-inch water pipe, house numbers in the 500s on both sides and fire hydrants. Atlantic Avenue leaves it at the top, New Freedom Road branches off diagonally towards the lower left, and the road to Lucastion leaves it towards the right near the bottom. Blocks 192 and 193 on the west side are long, deep lots with frame dwellings, stables and outbuildings facing the pike; the Watsontown public school, heated by stove with no lights, and the Watsontown Fire Company stand at the fork with New Freedom Road. On the east side, blocks 253 and 254 run back to the railroad with only a few dwellings and a store. The strip is sparsely built, with open land between houses.
notes: The road to Lucastion is today's United States Avenue at the White Horse Pike.

Placed with a helmert transformation from two junctions on the White Horse Pike (Atlantic Avenue and United States Avenue), 540 m apart; the New Freedom Road junction was not detected, and its OpenStreetMap node lies about 9 m from where this placement puts the drawn junction.

Two parts separated by a heavy line along the railroad, both turned with north to the right (about +72 to +77 deg). Part 1 (right, larger): Pine Grove, East Atlantic Av with Point Breeze, Albertson, Palethorp, Overington, Palmetto, Sepviva Avs, Clementon and Pilling's Lakes, Pine Valley Country Club golf grounds; top corner (Spring, Grove, Ivy, Forrest Avs, Lakeview) has no surviving junctions. Part 2 (left strip): Watsontown on the White Horse Pike, Atlantic Av, New Freedom Rd, Rd to Lucastion (United States Av). 100 ft.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers East Clementon and the ground north of it along Berlin Road, between Pillings Lake on the west and Rowand's Lake and Trout Run on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. Berlin Road runs down the page as a narrow strip and carries most of the building. In the top left, Wilson, Etlon, Delaware and Lake Avenues form a small grid of long, narrow lots in blocks 48 and 49, with scattered frame dwellings and poultry houses, and a dashed Public Road leads off to the south-west beside the lake. Delaware Avenue runs across to Berlin Road, where a 6 inch water pipe follows the road. Higgins (Forest) Avenue crosses the top right as a wide strip lined with narrow, unbuilt lots, with Harvard Terrace and Bungalow Avenue running off it, and across Trout Run is Erie Avenue. Below it is a wagon shed, two small sheds and John R. Rowand's charcoal plant with a grinding mill and stores beside Rowand's Lake. The middle of the sheet, blocks 50 and 51, is empty, and the compass lies in the blank ground. The lower third is the built-up part of East Clementon: Pawnee Avenue, Jerome Terrace, Narragansett Avenue, Smiths Terrace and Rancocas Avenue cross Berlin Road at right angles, with blocks 52 to 55 of numbered lots, a row of frame dwellings on each street and a few outbuildings. Lettering spread across the blocks reads East Clementon. The sheet joins sheets 4, 7, 10 and 16.
notes: Smiths Terrace is North Smith Terrace in OpenStreetMap; Higgins (Forest) is Higgins Avenue.

The control is weaker than the sheet looks: the four junctions on Berlin Road from Pawnee Avenue to Rancocas Avenue fit to 0.5 m, but the junctions in the top left (Berlin Road at Delaware and Higgins Avenues, Lake Avenue at Delaware and Etlon Avenues) lie 11 to 16 m from where that fit puts them, so the all-point fit has an RMSE of about 3.5 m.
Wilson Avenue, Harvard Terrace, Bungalow Avenue and Erie Avenue were not used as control.
The lettering across the lake at the left reads Pillings Lake in two parts.

East Clementon along Berlin Rd (Pawnee Av, Jerome Ter, Narragansett Av, Smiths Ter, Rancocas Av) with the Wilson, Etlon, Delaware, Lake Av grid and Higgins (Forest) at the top, John R. Rowand charcoal plant; north points right (+74 deg). 100 ft. One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the Clementon Heights tract east of Erial Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the right-hand edge of the page. The upper half is a regular subdivision of long narrow lots (numbered 84 to 153) laid out along Spruce, Walnut and Chestnut Lanes, which run across the sheet and are crossed by 1st Avenue at the left, Buttonwood Avenue and Evanson Avenue. Lakewood or Erial Avenue forms the lower edge of this grid; Davis Avenue and Tomlinson Avenue close it on the right as two diagonal streets, with Cherry Lane at the top. Blocks 83 to 87 hold scattered frame dwellings, a few named houses (Myrtle Wood, The Alma, Idyle Hour) and many empty lots. Along the lower side of Erial Avenue stand the Davis Textile Mill, with its electric power and fire-pump equipment noted, and a small group of dwellings. South of it the tract changes direction: Lakeview, Mt. Clement and Osborne Avenues run to the south-west, with deep lots and frame dwellings, and a Protestant Memorial Church with a light-oil heating store stands on the west side. Terrace Avenue crosses the lower right on a diagonal, with Pine Lane, Greenwood Avenue, Oak Lane, Summer Avenue and Grove Avenue running south from it and Hazel Lane and Highland Avenue to the east. Much of the south-eastern blocks (90 to 93, 199 and 255) is unbuilt, and a private road leads to the Lakeview house. A standpipe and a 6 inch and an 8 inch water pipe (1913) are marked at the right edge. Sheets 9 and 10 continue to the east and sheet 13 to the west; the neighbouring sheet numbers are lettered at the margins.
notes: Lakewood or Erial Avenue is now Erial Road.
Buttonwood Avenue between Evanson Avenue and 1st Avenue is now Diamond Avenue; 1st Avenue is West 1st Avenue.

Tomlinson Avenue appears to be the present Sitley Avenue (the street the modern line follows between Walnut and Chestnut Lanes); the modern Sitley Avenue curves away from the drawn street towards Highland Avenue.
Davis Avenue, Spruce Lane, Walnut Lane, Chestnut Lane, Hazel Lane, Highland Avenue and Terrace Avenue keep their names.
Control points drawn from the drawn street centres of the lanes are inconsistent with the modern grid by 3 to 8 m; the 1924 lane spacing and the angle of Evanson Avenue differ slightly from today's.
Davis Textile Mill stands on the south side of Erial Avenue.

Clementon Heights east of Erial Rd: Spruce, Walnut, Chestnut, Hazel Lanes, 1st, Buttonwood, Evanson, Davis, Tomlinson, Lakeview, Mt. Clement, Osborne, Terrace, Summer, Greenwood Avs; north right (+75 deg). 100 ft. One part. Junctions inconsistent by 3 to 8 m with modern streets.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 continues the Clementon Heights subdivision west of sheet 12, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned like it, so that north lies towards the right-hand edge of the page. The map is a series of very long, narrow blocks between parallel avenues, 7th Avenue at the left and 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd Avenues in order to the right, all running from the top of the sheet down to the lower edge. Lakewood Avenue or Erial Avenue crosses them at right angles about halfway down, and the lots are numbered along each avenue (blocks 106 to 115 above Erial Avenue and 107 to 115 below). Branch Avenue cuts across the upper left corner on a diagonal, and at the right edge Spruce Lane and Walnut Lane meet 2nd Avenue, where the blocks of sheet 12 begin. Building is thin: scattered frame dwellings, stables and sheds stand along the avenues and on the lots near Erial Avenue, and large parts of the blocks, especially in the north, are empty. Clementon Heights Public School stands in the upper left, St. Edward's Chapel (R. C.) with a hot-air heating note and the Clementon Heights Fire Co. hall stand beside Erial Avenue, and Hilltop Cottage lies further east. A 6 inch and an 8 inch water main is marked along Erial Avenue. At the lower right, Lakeview and Mt. Clement Avenues run off at an angle to the south-west, and the lower margin carries the scale bar and a note of no exposure. Heavy diagonal lines in the upper blocks mark property or tract boundaries rather than streets.
notes: Lakewood Avenue or Erial Avenue is now Erial Road.
The numbered avenues are today East and West 2nd to 7th Avenue, split at Erial Road; Branch Avenue is West Branch Avenue.
The drawn spacing of the avenues is about 4 percent wider than the modern street spacing (fitted scale 4.0 pixels per foot against about 3.9 on neighbouring sheets).
Most control lies along Erial Road, so the position across the sheet rests on the 7th Avenue / Branch Avenue and 2nd Avenue / Spruce Lane junctions.
Clementon Heights, 2nd to 7th Avs crossed by Lakewood Av or Erial Av, Branch Av at top left, Spruce and Walnut Lanes, Lakeview and Mt. Clement Avs; north right (+74 deg). 100 ft. One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the southern part of the Clementon Heights tract, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies towards the right-hand edge of the page. Two grids meet on it. In the upper left, long blocks run on a diagonal from the lower left to the upper right between Buttonwood, Cloverdale, Woodburn, Clearview and Branch Avenues, which are crossed by Forrester Avenue; blocks 205 to 210 and 118 are marked out in narrow lots, with a scatter of frame dwellings and many empty lots. Lakewood or Erial Avenue crosses the sheet from the upper left to the middle of the right side, bending near its middle from a diagonal to a straight run across the page, and divides the diagonal blocks from the rectangular ones to the south-east. There the numbered avenues run in order across the lower right, 7th Avenue at the right edge, then 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th Avenues, with deep lots numbered 100 to 150 and blocks 116, 234, 235 and 237. Pine runs across the lower left corner. Building is sparse and mostly small frame dwellings; a Union Church stands on Branch Avenue in the lower middle and a few named houses are lettered on lots at the right. The compass is drawn in the lower left corner, and the margins carry no-exposure notes where the area is unbuilt. Sheet 13 continues to the right of 7th Avenue, and sheet 15 adjoins the sheet on the left and upper left.
notes: Lakewood or Erial Avenue is now Erial Road, and its diagonal length is Clementon-Erial Road.

Buttonwood, Cloverdale, Woodburn, Clearview and Branch Avenues are now West Buttonwood, West Cloverdale, West Woodburn, West Clearview and West Branch Avenue; the numbered avenues are East and West 7th to 11th Avenue, split at Erial Road.
The Clearview Avenue and Branch Avenue junctions on the diagonal part of Erial Road are drawn about 15 percent closer together than the modern streets, and were left out of the control.
No control point lies in the upper left (diagonal) part of the sheet, which is placed by extrapolation from the right half.

Clementon Heights south: diagonal Buttonwood to Branch Avs and Forrester Av (upper left), 7th to 11th Avs (lower right), Lakewood or Erial Av, Pine; north right (+76 deg). 100 ft. One part; diagonal half without control, diagonal Clementon-Erial Rd junctions left out (drawn spacing 17 percent shorter).

sheet-15-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 15, the main map, covers the southern end of Clementon Heights, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points up and to the right. Pine runs across the top of the part, and from it Buttonwood, Cloverdale, Woodburn, Clearview and Branch Avenues run down and to the left through long blocks 238 to 243 of narrow lots, ending at the Turnersville & Berlin Road, which crosses the left side of the part diagonally beside the heavy line that divides it from part 2. In the lower right, Keyser Avenue, 13th Avenue, 12th Avenue and 11th Avenue lay out blocks 231 to 233 and 238 and 239, bounded at the bottom by Daniels Avenue. The subdivision is thinly built: one-storey and one-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings are scattered along every avenue, more of them near Pine and on 12th and 13th Avenues, with many lots still empty. There are no named works, churches or schools on the part. Sheet 14 continues beyond the top and right edges, and the area north-west of Pine is drawn as part 2 in the lower left corner of the sheet.
notes: Pine is today's Pine Street; the avenues carry East prefixes (East Buttonwood Avenue and so on); Keyser Avenue is Kayser Avenue; the Turnersville & Berlin Road is Turnersville-Hickstown Road.

The fit has 4.5 m RMSE: junctions near Keyser and Daniels Avenues sit 4 to 7 m from a uniform fit, and the part is drawn about 2 percent larger than the rest of the atlas. Junctions of Branch Avenue with 11th, 12th and 13th Avenues were left out (7 to 11 m residuals).

Two parts. Part 1 (main): Pine to Daniels Av, Buttonwood, Cloverdale, Woodburn, Clearview, Branch Avs, Keyser, 11th to 13th Avs, Turnersville & Berlin Rd; north up-right (+58 deg). Part 2 (lower left, behind a heavy line along Turnersville & Berlin Rd, own north arrow): the blocks north-west of Pine (Spring, Oak, Buttonwood, Lakewood or Erial Av, Cloverdale), drawn displaced from their true place beyond the top of part 1. 100 ft.

sheet-15-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 15 is the lower left corner of the sheet, cut off from the main map by a heavy line along the Turnersville & Berlin Road and given its own north arrow. It shows the blocks on the north-west side of Pine, which on the ground lie beyond the top edge of the main part, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing up and to the right. Spring and Buttonwood Avenue run up and to the right, crossed by Oak and by Lakewood or Erial Avenue; Cloverdale Avenue runs down to Pine at the bottom of the part, where the sheet notes that sheet 15 continues. The blocks, numbered 210, 211, 212, 219, 221, 222 and 223, are large and mostly empty; there are a handful of frame dwellings on Oak, along Lakewood or Erial Avenue and on Cloverdale Avenue. There are no named buildings or works.
notes: Lakewood or Erial Avenue is today's Clementon-Erial Road; Spring is West Spring Street, Oak is Oak Street and Pine is Pine Street.
The part is drawn displaced from its true position next to the main map; it has its own placement.

Two parts. Part 1 (main): Pine to Daniels Av, Buttonwood, Cloverdale, Woodburn, Clearview, Branch Avs, Keyser, 11th to 13th Avs, Turnersville & Berlin Rd; north up-right (+58 deg). Part 2 (lower left, behind a heavy line along Turnersville & Berlin Rd, own north arrow): the blocks north-west of Pine (Spring, Oak, Buttonwood, Lakewood or Erial Av, Cloverdale), drawn displaced from their true place beyond the top of part 1. 100 ft.

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 16, the largest part, shows the Amber Terrace development on the south side of Blackwood Avenue at the western edge of Clementon, west of the blocks on sheet 2. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north straight up the page and is separated from the other two parts of the sheet by a heavy line along its east and south sides. Blackwood Avenue runs across the top of the part. From it Wilson Road, De Cou Road and Woodrow Road run south through narrow lots, and Signal Hill Road runs south and then south-east at the east end. Ashelman Road crosses the part diagonally from the lower middle towards the north-east, cutting off a triangle of lots. The tract name Amber Terrace is lettered in large spaced capitals across the lots between Wilson Road and Woodrow Road. Building is light: a row of one-storey and one-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings along both sides of Wilson Road, a few dwellings and a store near Blackwood Avenue, a pump house and a 6,000 gallon stand pipe for the development's water supply east of Wilson Road, and only scattered dwellings further east. The lots east of Woodrow Road and around Signal Hill Road are laid out but almost empty, and the land west of the part is marked vacant beyond. None of the cross streets reaches another street within the part except at Blackwood Avenue.
notes: Blackwood Avenue is now Blackwood-Clementon Road.
De Cou Road corresponds in position to today's West Branch Avenue, and Woodrow Road to the street OpenStreetMap names Woordrow Avenue.
Ashelman Road is not in OpenStreetMap; the area south of Blackwood-Clementon Road has been rebuilt as apartments.
Placed with a helmert transformation from four junctions, all on Blackwood Avenue; the fitted scale is about 1 percent larger than the rest of the atlas.

Three parts separated by heavy lines. Part 1 (top left, largest): Amber Terrace on the south side of Blackwood Av west of sheet 2 (Wilson, De Cou, Woodrow, Ashelman, Signal Hill Rds), north up. Part 2 (right strip): west ends of Clementon Heights blocks, Davis Av, Cherry Lane, Evanson, Buttonwood, 1st, 2nd Avs, north up-left (-17 deg). Part 3 (bottom): Clementon Hill in East Clementon, Berlin Rd with Rancocas, Clementon, Mohawk Avs and Mercedes (arbitrary), north up-left (-16 deg). 100 ft "entire sheet". All three parts have junctions along one street only (helmert).

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 16 is a narrow strip along the east side of the sheet, separated from the other parts by a heavy line, and shows the western ends of the blocks of Clementon Heights next to those on sheets 12 and 13. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points up and to the left. Davis Avenue crosses the top of the strip diagonally, and Cherry Lane runs south from it to Evanson Avenue. Below follow Evanson Avenue, Buttonwood Avenue, 1st Avenue and 2nd Avenue, each running across the strip to the east edge, where the blocks continue on sheets 12 and 13. Blocks 82, 94, 95 and 96 are cut into narrow lots with a handful of frame dwellings, mostly on Evanson Avenue and 1st Avenue; block 82 between Davis Avenue and Evanson Avenue is largely empty apart from two dwellings near Davis Avenue. The west side of the strip, along the heavy dividing line, is marked as having no exposure. There are no institutions or works in the part.
notes: Buttonwood Avenue here lies where Diamond Avenue runs today, between Evanson Avenue and West 1st Avenue; 1st and 2nd Avenues are West 1st and West 2nd Avenue.
Placed with a helmert transformation from two junctions on Cherry Lane (Davis Avenue and Evanson Avenue).

Three parts separated by heavy lines. Part 1 (top left, largest): Amber Terrace on the south side of Blackwood Av west of sheet 2 (Wilson, De Cou, Woodrow, Ashelman, Signal Hill Rds), north up. Part 2 (right strip): west ends of Clementon Heights blocks, Davis Av, Cherry Lane, Evanson, Buttonwood, 1st, 2nd Avs, north up-left (-17 deg). Part 3 (bottom): Clementon Hill in East Clementon, Berlin Rd with Rancocas, Clementon, Mohawk Avs and Mercedes (arbitrary), north up-left (-16 deg). 100 ft "entire sheet". All three parts have junctions along one street only (helmert).

sheet-16-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 16 shows Clementon Hill, a development on the south side of Berlin Road in East Clementon, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points up and slightly to the left. A heavy line separates it from the other two parts of the sheet. Berlin Road crosses the part from west to east; on its north side lies block 51 and the end of Mercedes, a street lettered as an arbitrary name, running north-west. South of Berlin Road, Rancocas Avenue, Clementon Avenue and Mohawk Avenue run down the part through blocks 56 and 57 of narrow 30-foot frontage lots, with the tract name Clementon Hill lettered in spaced capitals across them. The East Clementon Fire Company's fire department building stands on Berlin Road at Rancocas Avenue, with a water tower nearby, and a water pipe is shown along Berlin Road and down Rancocas Avenue. The blocks hold a few dozen one-storey frame dwellings. Block 58 to the east is open, and the south edge of the part is marked as having no exposure.
notes: Mercedes is marked as an arbitrary name; no street of that name exists there today.
Placed with a helmert transformation from three junctions, all on Berlin Road.

Three parts separated by heavy lines. Part 1 (top left, largest): Amber Terrace on the south side of Blackwood Av west of sheet 2 (Wilson, De Cou, Woodrow, Ashelman, Signal Hill Rds), north up. Part 2 (right strip): west ends of Clementon Heights blocks, Davis Av, Cherry Lane, Evanson, Buttonwood, 1st, 2nd Avs, north up-left (-17 deg). Part 3 (bottom): Clementon Hill in East Clementon, Berlin Rd with Rancocas, Clementon, Mohawk Avs and Mercedes (arbitrary), north up-left (-16 deg). 100 ft "entire sheet".
